unit.name: Three pillars for AI career success
unit.description: Laurence lays out a career framework centered on technical depth, business focus, and delivery, then explains how output can steer interviews toward a candidate's strengths.
unit.summary: Laurence says candidates can no longer rely on simply listing AI on a resume; they must show evidence of three success pillars [ts=1753s]. The first pillar is understanding in depth: knowing machine learning, architectures, papers, and how to put research to work, while tracking trends with a good signal-to-noise ratio [ts=1835s]. The second is business focus, where hard work is measured by output rather than hours and output should be aligned with the job one wants [ts=1875s]. The third is bias toward delivery: ideas are cheap, execution matters, and grounded half-baked ideas can outperform fluffy unimplemented ones [ts=2126s].

key_points.text: Candidates must be able to show the three pillars, not merely claim AI experience.
Understanding in depth includes ML academics, model architectures, papers, and applying that knowledge.
Hard work is framed as output created, not simply hours spent.
Output should be for the job one wants, so interviewers ask about work the candidate understands.
Bias toward delivery is summarized by the idea that execution matters more than ideas alone.
